items.title: There's a surprising message from inside Iran after the ceasefire
items.description: While the bombs may have stopped inside Iran for now, Iranians who have been speaking with ABC News say the mood on the ground is anything but happy.

items.title: Live: US military to begin blockade of Strait of Hormuz at midnight tonight
items.description: US Central Command confirmed it will begin implementing a blockade of "all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports" starting at midnight tonight AEST. Follow live.

items.title: A new blockade, an unblocked oil pipeline and a Lebanon sticking point. What you need to know about Iran today
items.description: Donald Trump knows a US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will not increase fuel supply or bring down oil prices — but will it advance peace talks?

items.title: Trump ally Victor Orbán concedes 'painful' defeat in Hungary election
items.description: After 16 years in power, the powerful far-right leader says he will serve in opposition, with centre-right ⁠candidate Peter Magyar's Tisza Party ​on course for a super majority.

items.title: Canada has flipped the script on child care. Could Australia copy?
items.description: Australia definitely won't nationalise child care, even though the data suggests there's a strong case. Perhaps a more feasible idea would be to copy what Canada has done.

items.title: 'She just lost every coin flip': How a short hike went so wrong for Celine Cremer
items.description: Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer was on the trip of a lifetime, but on a hike in Tasmania she left the trail and was never seen again. It took a private investigator, a YouTuber, loved ones and an army of volunteers to find answers.

items.title: The underground 3D printing farms arming Ukraine's soldiers
items.description: In spare rooms and backyard sheds, volunteers across Europe are 3D printing drone bomb parts to supply Ukraine's military.

items.title: 'Like a flea on an elephant's back': The unexpected rise of solar power
items.description: Solar power is forecast to overtake coal as the world's biggest source of electricity next year, and its growth shows no signs of slowing down. Behind its success is a little-known Australian inventor.

items.title: Live: McIlroy makes his move, hunted by Scheffler and Rose in Masters finale
items.description: Rory McIlroy, hunting a second straight Masters victory, recovers from an early double bogey as three-time runner-up Justin Rose slips up after streaking to the top of the leaderboard in the final round at Augusta. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel crisis has some some delaying retirement and working from home
items.description: The COVID-19 pandemic brought job losses, working from home and economic instability. Some fear the US-Israel war on Iran and spiking fuel prices have created similar struggles.

items.title: Live: Albanese and Wong to visit Brunei and Malaysia to shore up fuel supply
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Brunei and Malaysia this week as part of efforts to shore up Australia's fuel and fertiliser supply. Follow live.

items.title: Heroes of Bondi stabbing awarded for their bravery two years on
items.description: Two years on from the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbing attack, eight heroes have been recognised in a special Australian Bravery Decorations honours list.

items.title: Caretaker files for possession of impressionist Frederick McCubbin's former country home
items.description: A court has heard claims the former home of an Australian impressionist is not safe to walk through, with "black mould, evidence of vermin and wheelie bins collecting rainwater".

items.title: Live: Markets on edge, oil set to rise on US Gulf blockade threats
items.description: The Middle East failed peace talks are expected to drive oil prices higher and reverse the anticipated gains on the ASX today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: The recycling project turning used tennis balls into shoes
items.description: What should be done with all those used tennis balls that get inevitably sent to landfill? Lilian Xu might have found the answer.

items.title: Quiz: Jump in, we're going back in time
items.description: Which state had Australia's only communist MP? And where did the Titanic sink?

items.title: How to make your workplace dog-friendly
items.description: How can employers design dog-friendly workplaces if they want to, and what does the law say about animals at work?

items.title: The 'extraordinary' rise of Kim Jong Un's mysterious teenage daughter
items.description: North Korea leader Kim Jong Un's 13-year-old daughter is tipped to be next in line. So who is Kim Ju Ae?

items.title: 'Missed opportunity': Astronomers lament loss of telescope partnership
items.description: The Artemis II mission used space technology developed in Australia, but experts fear the axing of a multimillion-dollar telescope partnership may stifle innovation and astronomy.

items.title: Cyclone Maila kills at least 11 people in Papua New Guinea
items.description: The Australian government will give $2.5 million to support relief and recovery efforts in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands after Tropical Cyclone Maila.

items.title: Mystery surrounds suspected people smuggler in WA's far-north
items.description: Months after the arrival of six Chinese nationals in one of Australia's most isolated communities, questions remain about another man suspected of attempting to assist them.

items.title: Domestic violence hotline can only answer 50 per cent of calls
items.description: More than $290 million in federal funding is on the table for domestic violence services nationwide, but Canberra providers are concerned about how it will be distributed and tracked by the ACT government.

items.title: Major setback for beekeepers as varroa mite chemical resistance detected again
items.description: There are growing fears that a second varroa mite strain could enter Australia, as beekeepers lose key chemical options for controlling the tiny parasites of honey bees.

items.title: An Aussie rugby win at home is one thing but victory in NZ is another
items.description: Australian teams will only boost their chances of achieving the ultimate success in Super Rugby Pacific if they conquer the challenge of beating their New Zealand opponents across the Tasman.

items.title: Sunny North Queensland set for more rain as ex-TC Maila tracks towards the coast
items.description: Beautiful one day, heavy rain, dangerous surf and frosts, the next — Queensland faces a mixed bag of weather throughout the state over the coming days.
